title: Stored target shares gave lower noise dimension than site shuffles in five of seven selected worm map models
abstract: We tested whether anatomical target shares affect noise dimension in seven public C. elegans brain maps. A fixed 162-cell panel and independent shared-site release gave a conditional model. Stored shares increased correlation participation dimension by 1.08 to 3.96 percent relative to equal shares at fixed retained site mass. The same shares, randomly assigned among each site's targets, gave higher mean dimension in all seven maps. Five maps passed correction for seven tests. Their observed dimensions were 0.79 to 1.87 percent below shuffle means. Two maps gave no clear separation. The direction persisted with two size rules. Raw covariance dimension gave a different equal-share comparison. These results concern assumed release events, not measured neural noise, coding performance or a developmental law. Unknown conductance gains, release dependence, partial tissue, selected cells and no matched activity data limit interpretation. Original code, aggregate results, checks, figures and pinned external retrieval steps support reproduction. External records are not bundled.
